- AMD’s FY2025 10-K/A corrects transposed growth figures in the Client revenue discussion for the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025—not the reported revenue itself. [S1]
- Original 10-K: Client revenue growth was attributed primarily to a 31% increase in processor unit shipments and a 15% increase in average selling price. [S6]
- Corrected 10-K/A: Unit shipments increased 15%, and average selling price increased 31%. The explanation still cites strong demand for AMD desktop and mobile Ryzen processors. [S1]
- Reported financial results are unchanged: Client net revenue remains $10.6 billion for FY2025 versus $7.1 billion for FY2024, with reported growth of 51%. AMD says the amendment changes no other items or disclosures. [S6] [S1] [S9]
- The amendment does not update later events. It explicitly excludes information or events after the original filing date, February 4, 2026, and does not update disclosures affected by subsequent events. [S1] [S9]

- Qualcomm recorded a $5.7 billion income-tax expense in Q4 FY2025 to establish a valuation allowance against federal deferred-tax assets. These assets represent amounts available to reduce taxes on future taxable income. [S10]

- The trigger was the July 2025 OBBB tax legislation, which restored immediate deductions for domestic R&D beginning in FY2026 and changed preferential taxation of foreign-derived income. Qualcomm consequently expected to become subject to the corporate alternative minimum tax (CAMT) beginning in FY2026. [S5]

- CAMT imposes a 15% federal minimum tax on adjusted financial-statement income, reduced by general business credits. Qualcomm expected to remain subject to CAMT perpetually and therefore no longer expected to realize substantially all its existing federal deferred-tax assets. That expected loss of future tax benefits drove the allowance. [S2]

- The $5.7 billion expense should not be read as an equal FY2025 cash-tax payment: it recognized reduced recoverability of future tax benefits, rather than a current payment of that amount. The filing separately identifies higher cash taxes during FY2023–FY2025 from mandatory domestic R&D capitalization—distinct from the valuation-allowance charge—and places expected CAMT exposure beginning in FY2026.
